title: Cure chronic hepatitis C across genotypes with finite oral therapy

concept.text: Eradicate chronic HCV infection using a finite, interferon-free oral regimen, with sustained virological response after treatment. Sofosbuvir enabled the transition; subsequent pan-genotypic combinations made cure routine across genotypes 1–6. Proposed completion test: FDA approval of an oral regimen covering HCV genotypes 1–6, supported by pivotal trials measuring undetectable or unquantifiable HCV RNA at least 12 weeks after treatment ends (SVR12). Test set by: FDA sets the approval decision; AASLD–IDSA defines SVR12 as 'consistent with cure of chronic HCV infection.' Reported achieved: FDA approved sofosbuvir (Sovaldi) on 6 December 2013; the pan-genotypic milestone was achieved by sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (Epclusa) approval on 28 June 2016. Sources given: [FDA Sovaldi approval documentation](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/204671Orig1s000AdminCorres.pdf) ; [FDA Epclusa approval package](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/208341Orig1s000Approv.pdf) ; [AASLD–IDSA assessment of HCV cure](https://www.hcvguidelines.org/guidance/monitoring-patients-who-are-starting-hcv-treatment-are-on-treatment-or-have-completed-therapy/).

page.title: Pan-genotypic oral therapy for chronic hepatitis C
page.definition: A finite course of oral drugs without interferon cures chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection across genotypes 1–6, genetically distinct groups of the virus. Cure means undetectable or nonquantifiable HCV RNA at least 12 weeks after treatment ends, termed sustained virologic response (SVR12).

goal.need: Hepatitis C caused an estimated 239,000 deaths worldwide in 2024, mostly from cirrhosis and liver cancer. Where the choice of medicine depends on genotype, patients need a separate test before they can start treatment. A pan-genotypic regimen removes that step and can bring treatment within reach where genotype testing is unavailable or unaffordable. Cure lowers the risks of liver cancer and liver-related death. Access to diagnosis and medicines remains limited.

statements.body: WHO recommends pan-genotypic antiviral treatment for chronic HCV infection.
statements.quote: WHO recommends therapy with pan-genotypic direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) for all adults, adolescents and children down to 3 years of age with chronic hepatitis C infection.

statements.body: The American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the Infectious Diseases Society of America identify virologic cure as the treatment goal.
statements.quote: The proximate goal of HCV therapy is SVR (virologic cure)

completion.title: One oral, interferon-free regimen achieves SVR12 in more than 85% of patients in each HCV genotype 1–6.
completion.criterion: For the same finite, interferon-free oral regimen in adults with chronic HCV infection, the observed SVR12 rate must exceed 85% separately in genotypes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6. Count a patient as having SVR12 when HCV RNA is undetectable or below the assay’s lower limit of quantification at least 12 weeks after treatment ends.
completion.set_by: World Health Organization Guidelines Development Group, 2018 chronic hepatitis C treatment guideline, section 4.2. AASLD–IDSA guidance defines SVR12.
completion.threshold_quote: Pangenotypic is defined as an SVR rate >85% across all six major HCV genotypes
completion.basis: In ASTRAL-1, -2 and -3, adults without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis received oral sofosbuvir/velpatasvir for 12 weeks. The numbers achieving SVR12 were 323/328 for genotype 1, 237/238 for genotype 2, 264/277 for genotype 3, 116/116 for genotype 4, 34/35 for genotype 5 and 41/41 for genotype 6. FDA approved the regimen on 28 June 2016. WHO published its numerical definition in 2018.

milestones.title: An HCV antiviral produces 50% and 90% inhibition of viral RNA replication in cell culture.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate concentration-dependent inhibition of HCV RNA replication in cell culture and determine the concentrations that produce 50% and 90% inhibition, EC50 and EC90.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 2017 HCV drug-development guidance, section III.A.1.b.
milestones.threshold_quote: 50 and 90 percent effective concentrations (EC50 and EC90) should be determined.

milestones.title: Two days of an oral HCV protease inhibitor lower plasma HCV RNA in infected people.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate a decline from baseline in plasma HCV RNA during two days of oral NS3 protease inhibitor monotherapy in a placebo-controlled study of people with chronic genotype 1 infection.
milestones.set_by: Boehringer Ingelheim and collaborating investigators, BILN 2061 proof-of-concept studies; the published test concerned genotype 1.
milestones.threshold_quote: BILN 2061 twice daily given as monotherapy for 2 days in 31 patients infected with chronic genotype 1 HCV infection

milestones.title: A finite interferon-free oral HCV regimen produces undetectable RNA 24 weeks after treatment.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate sustained virologic response after a 24-week course of oral sofosbuvir plus ribavirin in previously untreated adults with chronic genotype 1 infection. Measure the proportion with undetectable HCV RNA 24 weeks after treatment ends.
milestones.set_by: NIH investigators, the phase 2a protocol's primary efficacy endpoint, published by Osinusi and colleagues; the test concerned genotype 1.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary study end point was the proportion of participants with undetectable HCV viral load 24 weeks after treatment completion

milestones.title: Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir meets the pivotal ASTRAL SVR12 efficacy tests across HCV genotypes 1–6.
milestones.criterion: For adults without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis, 12-week sofosbuvir/velpatasvir achieves SVR12, HCV RNA <15 IU/mL. ASTRAL-1, covering genotypes 1, 2, 4–6, requires superiority to 85% by a two-sided exact binomial test at α=0.05. ASTRAL-2/3, covering genotypes 2/3, require the lower 95% confidence bound for the difference versus sofosbuvir/ribavirin to exceed −10 percentage points. FDA's 2016 review records success; responses were 618/624, 133/134 and 264/277, respectively.
milestones.set_by: FDA, accepted ASTRAL-1–3 protocol efficacy tests reproduced and evaluated in the NDA 208341 clinical review.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary hypothesis was that subjects in the SOF/VEL group would achieve an SVR12 rate superior to the performance goal of 85%,

milestones.title: FDA approves an interferon-free oral regimen for chronic HCV genotypes 2 and 3.
milestones.criterion: FDA approves an oral combination for chronic HCV infection whose prescribing information recommends interferon-free treatment for both genotype 2 and genotype 3. The labelled treatment durations may differ by genotype.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration: NDA 204671 approval letter and original Sovaldi prescribing information, December 2013, sections 1 and 2.1.
milestones.threshold_quote:
Genotype 2 SOVALDI + ribavirin 12 weeks
Genotype 3 SOVALDI + ribavirin 24 weeks

milestones.title: Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir exceeds an 85% pooled SVR12 rate in ASTRAL-1.
milestones.criterion: In adults with genotype 1, 2, 4, 5 or 6 infection and either no cirrhosis or compensated cirrhosis, test the pooled response to 12 weeks of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir. Show that the proportion with HCV RNA below 15 IU/mL 12 weeks after treatment exceeds 85% by a two-sided exact one-sample binomial test at α = 0.05. Include everyone who received at least one dose and count missing responses as failures.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, NDA 208341 clinical review of the ASTRAL-1 statistical analysis plan.
milestones.threshold_quote: superior to the performance goal of 85%, calculated using the 2-sided exact 1-sample binomial test at the 0.05 significance level.

milestones.title: Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir meets the 10-point SVR12 noninferiority margin for genotype 2.
milestones.criterion: In ASTRAL-2, compare 12 weeks of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir with 12 weeks of sofosbuvir plus ribavirin in adults with genotype 2 infection and either no cirrhosis or compensated cirrhosis. For the difference in SVR12 rates, investigational regimen minus comparator, the lower bound of the two-sided 95% confidence interval must exceed −10 percentage points. Adjust for cirrhosis and previous treatment. SVR12 requires HCV RNA below 15 IU/mL 12 weeks after treatment.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, NDA 208341 statistical review of the ASTRAL-2 analysis plan.
milestones.threshold_quote: the lower bound of the 95% CI on the difference was greater than -10%.

milestones.title: Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir meets the 10-point SVR12 noninferiority margin for genotype 3.
milestones.criterion: In ASTRAL-3, compare 12 weeks of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir with 24 weeks of sofosbuvir plus ribavirin in adults with genotype 3 infection and either no cirrhosis or compensated cirrhosis. For the difference in SVR12 rates, investigational regimen minus comparator, the lower bound of the two-sided 95% confidence interval must exceed −10 percentage points. Adjust for cirrhosis and previous treatment. SVR12 requires HCV RNA below 15 IU/mL 12 weeks after treatment.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, NDA 208341 statistical review of the ASTRAL-3 analysis plan.
milestones.threshold_quote: non-inferior to the rate for 24-week SOF + RBV by 10%.

results.finding: In ASTRAL-1–3, 12-week sofosbuvir/velpatasvir achieved SVR12 rates of 95–99% among 1,035 treated participants across HCV genotypes 1–6.
results.detail: Adults had no cirrhosis or compensated cirrhosis. ASTRAL-1 exceeded the 85% benchmark (p<0.001). ASTRAL-2's difference had a 95% CI of 0.2–10.3 percentage points; ASTRAL-3 was significantly superior to sofosbuvir/ribavirin. This review reports efficacy, not an approval decision.
results.quote:
Above 95% SVR12 rates for 12 weeks of SOF/VEL were observed in all three trials, ASTRAL-1 
to 3, and the SVR12 rates were significantly higher than the pre-specified threshold or the rate 
for the active control.

results.finding: Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir achieved SVR12 in 99% of 624 ASTRAL-1 recipients.
results.detail: ASTRAL-1's 618/624 responses satisfy the specified exact binomial test against 85%, inferred from the counts. ASTRAL-2/3 responses were 133/134 and 264/277; treatment-difference lower 95% confidence bounds were +0.2 and +9.6 percentage points, both above −10. All used 12-week treatment and HCV RNA <15 IU/mL.

results.finding: ASTRAL-1 adults with genotype 1 receiving sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (n=328) had 98.5% SVR12 from the reported counts.
results.detail: Table 30 prints 98.1% beside 323/328, which calculates to 98.5%. Both values exceed 85%.

results.detail: ASTRAL-2 separately reported 99.3% SVR12 (133/134) for the same regimen.
